newsitem.title: HUNGARY: CEO resigns as Cofinec regroups.
newsitem.headline: CEO resigns as Cofinec regroups.

text.p: The French-registered printed packaging company Cofinec S.A. said on Monday it finished a thorough review of its operations and that its chief executive Stephen Frater had resigned.
"Mr. Frater's resignation results from a mutual recognition of the need of an increased industrial focus in the group," Cofinec said in a statement.
The company said it is seeking Frater's successor, adding it planned further changes in the management.
Cofinec announced two weeks ago that it posted lower net profits in the first six months of 1996 than in the same period of last year primarily due to its performance in Hungary.
Net profit for the first half of this year was 2.1 million French francs, down from 10.3 million French francs in the first half of 1995, the company said.
Cofinec added in the statement it had finished a review of its operations and it sees higher costs than previously expected.
"Inventory levels are high and costs of bringing the new Cofinec Polska operations on stream will exceed previous expectations," Cofinec said.
The company said it anticipates the need of establishing reserves of 20 million French francs against the inventory.
The contribution of the Polish subsidiary to revenues for 1996 will fall short of Cofinec's forecast by 18 million francs, it said.

Cofinec plans to merge its two principal Hungarian operating subsidiaries, the printing houses Petofi and Kner, to increase efficiency and cut costs. Restructuring costs will amount to some 22 million francs, for which Cofinec will separate reserves.
Cofinec said Carlos Barbero, an executive of the packaging company Tetra-Pak will join Cofinec as Chief Financial Officer.
The management will propose to the shareholders to abolish the supervisory board, and only keep the board of directors, to strengthen the management further, Cofinec said.

Pehr Gyllenhammar, chairman of the supervisory board has indicated his willingness to take over the post of chairman of the board of directors in a one-level management structure, but has limited his term to 12 months, the statement added.
Cofinec closed at 4,000 forints on the Budapest Stock Exchange, up 100 forints.
